label: Plan · open dinner
title: Make tonight the clear starting point.
summary: A quieter frame gives the dinner decision, cook, and next action a stronger hierarchy.
keep: Keep the selected-day model, personal greeting, explicit cook identity, and quick eating-out option.
notes: Spend less space on the frame
The brand masthead, greeting, and tall date strip repeat orientation before the decision.
Use one compact Plan header, a quieter greeting, and smaller day tiles.
Hierarchy · Put the task earlier.
One dominant next step
Two large side-by-side actions have almost equal visual weight.
Make Choose a meal primary. Keep Eating out directly beneath as an obvious secondary action.
Choice clarity · Preserve both paths.
Suggested is not assigned
The suggestion is correctly labelled, but Change can imply that someone is already assigned.
Pair the suggested person with Assign. Use Change only after a cook is assigned.
Honest status · Avoid implied commitment.
Useful context, less ceremony
Weather and a large zero-count log consume substantial space in the open state.
Keep weather compact. Use a small explanatory empty history rather than prominent zeros.
Proximity · Keep the dinner decision dominant.

label: Plan · planned dinner
title: Food, person, action—in one glance.
summary: Bound the photo and bring the cooking responsibility and primary action into one coherent block.
keep: Keep food photography, the assigned cook, serving count, and date-specific actions.
notes: Keep the day selector compact
The tall opening stack consumes space before a planned meal appears.
Retain seven visible days in a shorter, quieter row; clearly distinguish selected and today.
Orientation · Selection stays explicit.
Give the photo a job
The photo and separate title consume much of the card, especially on smaller phones.
Cap the image height and keep title, date, and image tightly grouped.
Balance · Food still leads.
Group practical facts
Cook identity and servings occupy separate vertical bands.
Keep the assigned person near time and servings, immediately above the action.
Proximity · Know who, how long, and how much.
Match the action to the moment
Today, future, and completed dinners need different emphasis.
Use Start cooking, View recipe, or a cooked confirmation with Share as the next step. Try the state selector.
Feedback · Completion changes the interface.

label: Weather & household
title: Context that earns its place.
summary: Weather, dinner history, and household activity should be compact, specific, and honest about what is recorded.
keep: Keep the corrected, contrasting Apple Weather attribution. The older reference image predates that fix; the proposal preserves it.
notes: Treat weather as one small unit
The weather region uses a large title, separate values, and a generous attribution gap.
Group condition, high/low, and rain chance. Retain readable official attribution and its link. The logo here is a layout placeholder.
Density · Weather supports the plan.
Name whose history this is
Your dinner log can sound personal when the counts represent shared household dinners.
Label it Household dinners and state the period and recorded total. Never infer unlogged meals.
Trust · Explain the scope of numbers.
Give activity a human subject
Household activity needs to connect a face, person, action, and relevant meal without becoming a dashboard.
Use compact actor-and-action rows, with a secondary time and day. Use real photos when available; initials here are sample fallbacks.
Recognition · Show what changed and who did it.
End with useful continuity
Supporting modules can become a long sequence of headings and empty space.
Use a quiet tomorrow preview and a clear caught-up ending. Keep all other days outside today’s dinner area.
Closure · Make the end of the screen intentional.

label: The Table
title: Let the people and posts lead.
summary: Reduce the introduction above the feed, bound the media, and make post actions familiar.
keep: Keep the private audience, household filter when meaningful, media, comments, and chronological context.
notes: Quiet the privacy explanation
A large privacy card, title, and filter occupy much of the first viewport.
Use one compact audience line with People. Treat the filter as a view of posts, not as a change of recipient.
Hierarchy · Reach the first post sooner.
Create a repeatable post anatomy
The first large image takes nearly the remainder of the screen; caption and actions are below it.
Use author, bounded media, actions, then caption. Respect media aspect ratios within a sensible height limit.
Rhythm · Make the feed easy to scan.
Use one reaction language
Posts use a plate metaphor while comment reactions use a heart.
Use hearts for post and comment reactions. Keep bookmarking distinct from liking.
Familiarity · Less decoding.
Make posting status legible
A visual mockup alone cannot prove that other people have received a post.
Distinguish waiting, sending, sent, and retry states; retain the draft while offline. Show new content without pull-to-refresh.
Feedback · Delivery must be honest.

label: Create menu
title: Two clear doors into creation.
summary: A post can already contain a question or poll. The creation menu should reflect that model.
keep: Keep a global entry for creation, recipe import routes, and questions/polls within the Table.
notes: Stop splitting one intention
Post to the Table and Ask the Table overlap, since posts can already include questions.
Offer one Post to the Table entry for food, places, ingredients, photos, and questions.
Choice clarity · Remove an unnecessary decision.
Keep recipes a distinct object
Recipes have structure and import tools that differ from social posts.
Give Add a recipe its own clear entry with a short description of import methods.
Mental model · Different tools for different objects.
Make a poll a post tool
The Ask route duplicates the generic composer while suggesting a separate content system.
Place Add poll inside the composer. Mention it here only as a quiet hint.
Progressive disclosure · Complexity when needed.
Make contextual creation direct
A global + forces the same menu regardless of where the user is.
On the Table, open a new post. In Recipes, add a recipe. Keep the global menu where intent is ambiguous.
Efficiency · Respect the current task.

label: New post
title: Give the thought more room than the form.
summary: The current freeform model is right. Refine its hierarchy, attachment controls, and draft feedback.
keep: Keep generic posts, optional photos/titles/tags/polls, private audience, and persistent drafts. The old Share dish restriction is already gone.
notes: Compress repeated context
Author, audience, and the privacy sentence form three separate lines before writing begins.
Use a compact author-and-audience row. Explain privacy once near posting.
Hierarchy · Begin with expression.
Let the writing breathe
A placeholder and a separate multi-line explanation compete for attention.
Use one inviting prompt. Keep examples as quiet help instead of another required-looking section.
Focus · The story is the main event.
Attach tools to the content
Large two-column tool rows read like additional form steps.
Use a compact attachment strip. Put photo edit/remove controls on the photo itself. Keep title in More.
Proximity · Controls belong to what they affect.
Show drafts and posting deliberately
The long empty sheet can make the bottom action feel disconnected from the work.
Keep a stable posting action and explicit draft status; preserve content when closing. The preview demonstrates local states only.
Confidence · No lost writing.

label: Post & comments
title: A conversation that reads naturally.
summary: Reduce the scaffolding around each reply while keeping attribution, reactions, and delivery status clear.
keep: Keep comment reactions, replies, deleted-parent context where needed, and the thread overflow. The misplaced top-level Save button is already removed.
notes: Bring the conversation closer
A large post title and isolated plate reaction separate the text from the comments.
Use a compact post summary and a familiar reaction row before the thread.
Reading flow · Less intervening chrome.
Anchor reactions to comments
Name, time, reply, heart, and overflow create multiple horizontal bands.
Group author and text; keep time/reply subdued and the reaction beside its comment. Highlight a notification’s target briefly.
Proximity · Easier attribution.
Use nesting instead of repetition
Each nested reply repeats a long Replying to name line.
Indent one level with a subtle thread line. Collapse longer branches behind View replies. Retain deleted context only when replies need it.
Density · More conversation, less labelling.
Make the reply target unmistakable
The bottom composer does not visually explain the distinction between a new comment and a targeted reply.
Show Replying to Alessandra directly above the field with Cancel. Keep sending/retry status on the affected reply.
Error prevention · Know who receives the reply.

label: Activity & notifications
title: Timely, contextual, and trustworthy.
summary: A notification should explain who did what, open the right place, and retain a meaningful unread state.
keep: Keep actor identity, unread markers, event time, and deep links. Phone delivery and multi-account sync still require real-device verification.
notes: Separate read from cleared
Clear all is the prominent header action. Current exit handling marks the filtered list read, including unseen rows.
Offer Mark all read; put clearing in overflow. Opening or actually viewing an item should determine individual read status.
User control · Do not erase attention silently.
Add the object and useful context
Rows rely heavily on full bold sentences and often omit the content being referenced.
Use actor + action + object, a short comment excerpt, and a specific household-joined event. Open the exact post/comment.
Recognition · No guessing what changed.
Group low-urgency reactions
Independent reactions can turn activity into noisy repeated events.
Group related reactions while keeping comments, replies, and joins distinct. Use thumbnails where they help recognition.
Signal · Preserve meaningful events.
Design delivery as a full journey
Your reported updates appeared only after refreshing; a better list alone does not solve that.
Require automatic foreground updates, deduplicated push, accurate badges, and correct deep links. The lock-screen state illustrates copy, not a delivery guarantee.
Reliability · This needs implementation and device evidence.

label: Household
title: Make belonging and responsibility obvious.
summary: Put people and cooking responsibilities before decoration, with explicit membership and invitation states.
keep: Keep the separated header controls from the recent fix, household identity, member management, and cook rotation.
notes: Use an unmistakable settings control
The header is improved, but the sliders symbol still reads as a filter or adjustment control.
Use a gear with a labelled accessibility action. Keep the household title and control separate. Bound the cover photo.
Familiarity · Settings should look like settings.
Let membership carry the screen
A large cover can delay the people list; initials may mask a missing-photo problem.
Prioritize name, role, real synced avatar, and meaningful recent activity. Initials here are explicit sample fallbacks, not evidence that photo sync is fixed.
Identity · A shared household must feel shared.
Choose instead of cycling
The current rotation changes the cook immediately when a day is tapped.
Open an explicit picker with every member and Unassigned, then save. Avoid accidental changes while exploring.
Error prevention · Make responsibility intentional.
Make the invitation state singular
Earlier removal and re-invitation messaging contradicted itself in your screenshots.
Treat pending, joined, removed, and new invitation as distinct states. A new invitation must explain that it can restore access.
Trust · One coherent message per state.

label: Profile
title: A person before a scoreboard.
summary: Bring identity and real contribution forward, and let milestones remain a quieter layer.
keep: Keep the photo/name, household association, privacy rules, editable self-profile, and Posts label.
notes: Scale identity to the task
The large banner, overlapping avatar, edit action, and name take substantial height.
Use a strong but compact avatar/name/role group. Keep editing obvious on your own profile only.
Hierarchy · Recognize the person quickly.
Make recent contribution specific
An activity section can read as an empty report instead of a useful sign of participation.
Show the latest verified action, date, and a small set of plain-language counts. Do not imply online presence without evidence.
Meaning · Activity should tell a story.
Keep milestones secondary
Large awards interrupt the route from identity to posts.
Summarize earned milestones in one quiet row with a separate detail destination.
Restraint · Celebration without obstruction.
Bring their content upward
The content tabs begin near the bottom of the first screen.
Move posts and recipes higher. Keep saved/private collections visible only to the appropriate person.
Utility · See what they shared.

label: Recipe library
title: An inviting library, with less visual noise.
summary: Keep the editorial food photography while making titles, metadata, and controls more consistent.
keep: Keep the serif identity, two-column library at standard sizes, search, favorites, and source attribution.
notes: Get to the collection sooner
The masthead and large Recipe book title take two substantial rows.
Use one compact Recipes header and bring search directly beneath it.
Efficiency · The collection is the destination.
Tighten title and metadata rhythm
Different title lengths, category lines, and Added by lines create uneven cards.
Use a consistent title scale and concise time/source line. Allow wrapping, then align each row deliberately.
Rhythm · Easier scanning.
Quiet the favorite affordance
Large opaque circular favorite controls dominate the photo corners.
Keep a full touch target, but use a smaller glyph and quieter backing; preserve clear selected state.
Restraint · Controls support the food.
Design the missing-photo state
A no-photo recipe should not look broken or repeat the title inside a large placeholder.
Use a deliberate, restrained placeholder or compact text treatment. Do not invent a photo. Try the no-photo state and scroll.
Completeness · Empty assets deserve a design.

label: Recipe detail
title: Make the recipe useful before it gets long.
summary: Balance the hero image with the facts and ingredients someone needs to decide or cook.
keep: Keep serving adjustment, ingredients, source/author, favorites, and a contextual primary action.
notes: Bound the hero
The large photo delays the title, facts, and ingredients.
Use a shorter hero, then a clear title with time and servings immediately below.
Hierarchy · Beauty and utility together.
Remove empty metadata
A large Effort: Not set field consumes space without helping the decision.
Omit unset optional values. Keep source, authorship, and edit/share actions secondary but accessible.
Signal · Every prominent detail earns its place.
Support quick jumps
Ingredients and later sections require scrolling through the full document.
Add clear ingredients/directions/notes anchors; keep serving changes near ingredients. Maintain readable quantities.
Navigation · Reduce searching while cooking.
Use the right primary action
Planning, viewing tonight’s recipe, and cooking are different contexts.
Show Plan a night for an unplanned recipe and Start cooking for tonight. Keep the action reachable without hiding content.
Context · No generic action everywhere.

label: Groceries
title: Make more of the shopping list visible.
summary: The shopping task should dominate; date settings and export are supporting tools.
keep: Keep the already-collapsed shopping options, ingredient provenance, category grouping, and export capability.
notes: Compress the shopping window
A large date card and tall title delay the first shopping row.
Use one compact date range with Change, followed by a quick add field.
Hierarchy · Start shopping sooner.
Keep row hierarchy simple
Rows already include useful meal provenance, but strong type and trailing information icons add weight.
Lead with item and quantity; keep provenance on a quiet second line and details accessible on demand.
Scannability · Name first, explanation second.
Move export out of the main task
The fixed footer gives Reminders almost as much prominence as the shopping state.
Place export and shopping options in overflow. Keep direct addition and checking as the primary tasks.
Focus · Export is optional, shopping is central.
Use a smaller progress surface
The large fixed panel repeats an icon, count, instruction, and progress bar while covering rows.
Use a compact count/progress strip and contextual Undo after a check. Never make a checked item vanish without recovery.
Space + recovery · More list, less panel.

label: Cooking mode
title: Designed for hands that are busy.
summary: Give the active cooking task priority and move reflection to the end.
keep: Keep ingredient access, timers, completion logging, and optional notes. The step state uses illustrative text, not a recipe edit.
notes: Clarify the top controls
A bare minus and prominent End action create ambiguity during an active session.
Use a clear minimize affordance and put secondary session options in overflow. Give the recipe name and serving context a stable home.
Error prevention · Avoid accidental endings.
Show what helps when steps are missing
The empty-steps explanation sends the user through another All ingredients button.
Display ingredients directly when there are no instructions. For recipes with steps, use a focused step view.
Adaptation · An incomplete recipe stays useful.
Keep timers practical
A large timer panel and note form compete with the active cooking task.
Use a readable timer with clear pause/options; defer reflection until completion. Keep alerts and timer state explicit.
Focus · Support the task in progress.
Finish, then reflect
A note-for-next-time field appears before the user finishes cooking.
Confirm the saved dinner first, then offer a note and optional sharing. Make Undo available in the completed Plan state.
Closure · A clear and recoverable finish.

label: iPad layout
title: Use the width to reduce the work.
summary: A tablet deserves a composed layout, not a stretched phone screen.
keep: Keep the same navigation, selected day, meal model, and brand. This is an adaptive layout, not a separate product.
notes: Keep navigation human-sized
The phone composition expands across the tablet’s available width.
Keep the date rail at a comfortable width and use restrained page margins.
Scale · Control reading and reach.
Give dinner a main column
A wide hero can become the dominant use of the screen.
Constrain the meal card and image to a main column with cook and action immediately below.
Composition · A clear visual anchor.
Place context beside the task
Supporting weather and history continue vertically below the meal.
Use a second column for compact weather and household history. Keep related facts together.
Space · More useful information in view.
Adapt instead of shrinking
A fixed two-column layout would be inappropriate in Split View or large accessibility text.
Collapse to one column at narrow widths and larger type sizes; keep touch targets and reading order intact. Native reflow testing remains required.
Accessibility · Layout follows available space.
